quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce your chance of being in a crash?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: To reduce your chance of a crash, make yourself as visible as possible. Wear bright clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the right part of your lane.
Move to the left part of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.
Do not signal, as it may distract the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. Signal your intention and check for traffic. Pass only when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as close to the operator as comfortable, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes all work. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: What can help other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle to be seen clearly at intersections. Keep space around your bike so you can avoid a crash if needed.

questions.question: You are riding in traffic and a small animal enters your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as fast as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into other traffic is more dangerous than hitting a small animal.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is usually operated with the right foot.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not work as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always use your headlight when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you stay safe on the road. It helps you see and be seen better, avoid other drivers' blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: When going through a turn on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When making a turn, look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Keep your arms slightly bent on the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of accidents between motorcycles and other vehicles. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Motorists entering a highway from an entrance ramp to your right may not see your motorcycle. To help the entering drivers, you should:

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it, if needed.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles merging onto the highway from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let the vehicle safely enter the highway.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes to see if traffic is nearby.

questions.question: When riding in a group, it is best to put inexperienced riders near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can easily watch them.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and dealing with the most urgent ones first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which ones to handle first. Always use your headlight so others can see you. Keep adequate space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk forward and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle may speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk forward and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handlebar. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding side by side?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections can make it hard for riders to see.
Riding side by side does not give riders enough room to avoid hazards.
Riders on the left side have difficulty exiting the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding side by side does not give riders enough room to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists in a group should not ride side by side. Riders need enough space to maneuver and avoid hazards.
